purpose: Offline lookup before retrying a failed CCS/DSS operation. A lookup never connects, halts, resets, builds or loads.

groups.action: Correct the named argument or incompatible switch combination shown in REASON. Run the intended skill entry with explicit project and mode; do not retry target access until the command is valid.

Inspect this run's CSV, verdict.txt and CHECK lines. Verify expected count, array layout, value range and firmware counters. Preserve the captured values with FAIL; do not reload merely to obtain a passing verdict.
Repair the local skill/CCS installation or firmware contract, then rerun the offline audit and sync platform copies. A missing script or invalid contract is not evidence of a board fault.
Read the compiler and linker diagnostics in build.log, correct the project/toolchain configuration, then rebuild the exact selected output. Do not download the previous artifact.
Inspect the DSS/loadti log and the latest probe and session status. Distinguish USB enumeration from a verified DSS connection; observe the recovery interval and avoid repeated immediate loads.
Inspect the current session and round log. Confirm authorization before any load; for a read failure, keep the last CSV and FAIL verdict, and diagnose the retained DSS session before retrying.

errors.NO_PROBE: The learned wait checks Windows enumeration in 5 s steps and stores timing in probe-wait.json. A PnP hit does not prove driver access. Stop-to-verified-DSS timing is learned separately in probe-driver-wait.json, keyed by selected ccxml; a pre-load connect failure adds 5 s and gets one fresh-process retry. The next cycle bisects the last failed and successful intervals. Actual seconds vary by probe and require board measurement. Do not diagnose cable or power from one early NO_PROBE result. Measured 2026-11-18 (F28379D/XDS100v2): one check printed 'PROBE : NOT FOUND' + exit 3 while the operator was still plugging the probe in; the SAME command later printed 'XDS100 Class Debug Port', 'XDS100 Class Auxiliary Port', 'XDS100 Class USB Serial Port (COM11)' and RESULT: OK. Re-run once before touching hardware.
errors.PROBE_REENUMERATION: Observed on one XDS100v2 setup: the probe temporarily dropped out of PnP after DSS exited, then re-enumerated. Other adapters may differ. Windows enumeration and DSS driver access have separate timing records keyed by the selected target configuration; a new load requires verified DSS access.
errors.CONNECT_FAILED: A normal return from connect is insufficient. Require target.isConnected(true) and a target query. If connect failed before any load, the skill records elapsed Stop-to-connect failure, adds 5 s and retries once in a fresh DSS process. A later success bounds the next bisection estimate; repeated failures require log inspection, not an automatic hardware diagnosis.
errors.AMBIGUOUS_CORE: FIXED 2026-11-16: selection is automatic now. One C28xx core -> use it; several (F28379D is dual-core) -> use C28xx_CPU1 and log which was chosen; only when nothing is identifiable does it report USAGE + exit 2 with the enumerated names. This used to block every -Start on a dual-core part.
errors.CORE_UNVERIFIED: The retained DSS service did not record an exact CPU name, or the read requested another CPU. Refuse the read; select one core explicitly for a new approved load.
errors.CORE_MISMATCH: FIXED 2026-11-16: getListOfCPUs() returns the short name (C28xx_CPU1) while getCPUName() returns the full path (Texas Instruments XDS100v2 USB Debug Probe_0/C28xx_CPU1). The old strict !== compared those two and reported a mismatch for the CPU it had just opened. Now compared by substring containment.
errors.-1138: Device refused debug mode. An approved load is retried once in a fresh DSS process; measured 2026-11-15 at loads #35/#37/#44. A second failure needs DSS log and probe recovery analysis; it does not alone prove a board fault.
errors.-1133: Device blocked debug access because it is currently executing non-debuggable code. Measured 2026-11-18 on F28379D/XDS100v2: this is the realtime options (PoliteRealtimeMode=true, needed for run-time reads) being refused, not a dead board. It happens at CONNECT, so every later loadProgram in that run is impossible too. dssConnectVerified retries once with PoliteRealtimeMode and AllowInterruptsWhenHalted off; the log then shows 'DSS: PoliteRealtimeMode off, retrying connect for -1133' -> 'DSS: connected (realtime off)'. What follows may still fail: measured 2026-11-18 the reset then hit -6310 and lost the link, and only the reconnect branch (3 tries, 900/1800/2700 ms backoff) reached 'DSS: reset after reconnect (try 3)' -> 'DSS: loaded'. Judge success by 'DSS: loaded', not by the connect line. The options live in the DSS session, not on the board: a NEW download process starts with realtime on again and re-degrades by itself, so nobody has to switch it off by hand. loadti succeeds in the same minute because it never sets them, not because it turns something off. If loadti also reports -1133, the realtime setting is not the cause - first check the log for whether the degrade actually ran ('DSS: PoliteRealtimeMode off'), then look for a reset loop, non-debuggable code or the other core. Measured 2026-11-18: this -1133 was caused by the skill's own realtime options and disappeared once the realtime-off retry existed, so it must NOT be recorded as a Flash/erase or 'CPU running away' state. Never diagnose hardware from -1133 alone.
errors.LOAD_FAILED: memory.loadProgram failed on every attempt. Read server.log for the real code on stdout - the Java exception only says 'emulation failure'. Measured 2026-11-18: -1041 on the first write block means a fragmented .text (run check_ram_layout.ps1 and look for [BAD]); a Flash-linked .out in a RAM-only project can also fail here. -150/flash-operation and -6310 lines that appear BEFORE 'DSS: connected' are GEL/probe noise, not load failures.
errors.INVALID_READ_REQUEST: The -Variables/-Heartbeat path failed the identifier pattern, or Rounds/IntervalMs/WarmupMs were invalid. Measured 2026-11-18: 'pwsh -File script.ps1 -Variables ''a'',''b''' delivers ONE string that still contains the quotes, and hits this check. Use -Variables a,b (no quotes; the script splits on commas) or invoke in-process with the call operator so the array is real.
errors.VALUE_READ_FAILED: The debugger could not evaluate one expression. Measured 2026-11-18 on F2837xD: 'identifier not found: AdcRegs' and 'member ADCTRL1 not found' are 2833x names - F2837xD uses AdcaRegs.ADCCTL1/ADCCTL2/ADCSOC0CTL. EPwm*Regs.CMPA.all can come back as a >16-bit combined value (128122880 etc. against TBPRD=4999); read .bit.CMPA instead. Check the exact spelling against this build's .map before blaming the target.
errors.-151: SC_ERR_FTDI_OPEN / 'no XDS100 is plugged in, invalid serial, faulty USB cable'. Measured 2026-11-18 on a dual-XDS100 machine: xds100serial -l says 'No XDS100 emulators were found' while PnP has one OK probe plus a string of Unknown/Present=False ghosts. Root cause: .ccxml had no <Emulator Selection> by serial, so the default 'Only one XDS100' opened a ghost -> D2XX open failed. Fix: add <property Type="choicelist" Value="1" id="Emulator Selection"> with the real serial (from xds100serial, or COM port InstanceId minus its trailing char, e.g. ...TI90I42AB -> TI90I42A). Order per other-devices-and-probes.md §3.1: serial first, then cable/port, power, driver. NOTE: ti_c2000_set_probe.ps1 used to DELETE the device/router/other drivers when rewriting .ccxml, causing 'invalid processor ID'; FIXED 2026-11-18 - it now preserves all nodes (test_set_probe_bruteforce.ps1).
errors.-1041: The emulator lost target access. Stop the load loop, release the DSS session cleanly and verify the probe before retrying.
errors.-150: Probe/driver is not ready - OR GEL noise, which is the more common case. Judge by position in server.log (measured 2026-11-18, F28379D/XDS100v2): '-150 One of the FTDI driver functions ... invalid status' together with 'flash operation: Target failed to read 0x05F05E@Program' that appears BEFORE 'DSS: connected' is the emulation package/GEL probing during connect; the same run then reaches 'DSS: connected' -> 'DSS: reset' -> 'DSS: loaded' and the program runs, so nothing is wrong. Measured 2026-11-18 in one session: three -150 memory reads (0x5F05E/0x5F060/0x7026D) before 'DSS: connected', then one '-150 JTAG Communication Error' AFTER the link was up - and the run still reached 'DSS: loaded' and executed. So position is not a verdict either. Judge by effect: if the operation the user needs (connect, write, verify) still succeeds, it is transient FTDI noise; investigate only when the same operation keeps failing with -150, when 'Target failed to write ...' appears, or when the probe leaves PnP - then allow re-enumeration and a usable probe check instead of reconnecting immediately.
errors.RESET_FAILED: A reset exception alone is recoverable. Measured 2026-11-18 (F28379D/XDS100v2): -6310 plus 'Target reset failed. Error: -1' left the link dead ('target is not connected' from GEL), so dssResetVerified disconnected and retried connect up to 3 times with 900/1800/2700 ms backoff; try 3 printed 'DSS: reset after reconnect (try 3)' and then 'DSS: loaded'. When the link stays valid it instead halts once and continues to load. Refuse only when both paths fail.
errors.-6310: Failed CPU Reset: PRSC module failed to read a register. Measured 2026-11-18 on F28379D/XDS100v2 this arrived together with -150 memory reads and ended in 'Target reset failed. Error: -1' with the link lost - it is not by itself a board failure. The reconnect branch (3 tries, 900/1800/2700 ms backoff) recovered on try 3 and the image loaded. Do not loop -Start by hand; let the reconnect path finish and read the lines after it.
errors.STOP_UNCLEAN: The DSS stop marker was not written. Treat the session as failed and do not start another load automatically.
errors.PROBE_NOT_READY: DSS exited but the probe has not passed Windows enumeration. Wait, then separately confirm DSS access; a PnP hit is not driver-open proof.
errors.STALE_ARTEFACT: The exact selected .out predates a project source, linker input or build configuration. Rebuild and stage that output; also verify linked sources outside the project.
errors.STALE_MAP: CHANGED 2026-11-16: a map/out timestamp gap is now a NOTE, not a refusal. The map may describe a different build; the readers report it as source metadata and the data judgements still run. Previously this blocked a download the board could accept.
errors.RAM_PROOF_UNAVAILABLE: The selected image lacks a pinned map, RAM updater symbol or RAM counter. Reported as metadata; it no longer blocks the read.
errors.RAM_PROOF_NOT_ADVANCING: CHANGED 2026-11-16: reported as a boolean result (advancing=True/False) next to the data, not as a veto. A frozen RAM counter means the target may be halted - that is information about the target, not proof that the samples are wrong.
errors.READ_INCOMPLETE: A read began but did not finish all checks. Do not reuse the previous CSV or success verdict; inspect the child log and retry only after diagnosing the cause.
errors.STALE_SERVICE: The running session's recorded .out SHA256 differs from the selected file. Deliver captured data with a FAIL identity verdict; an approved new load is needed only if the user wants to run the newer image.
errors.TARGET_NOT_CONNECTED: A live DSS process is not proof of an accessible target. Refuse the read and diagnose the link.
errors.FW_ID_MISMATCH: The live firmware identity differs from the one recorded at load. This is a DATA judgement: the samples are still written, but the verdict says FAIL so they must not be trusted.
errors.FW_ID_UNREADABLE: Firmware identity is unavailable. Deliver captured data with a FAIL identity verdict until the image contract supplies it.
errors.HEARTBEAT_FAIL: The application counter is not advancing. This is a DATA judgement: samples are still written, the verdict says FAIL.
errors.NOT_RAM_IMAGE: CHANGED 2026-11-16: the location (RAM or FLASH) is reported as SOURCE metadata and ramLinked=True/False; it no longer refuses the read. Running from Flash is a legitimate state that changes what the addresses mean.
errors.BUF_CHANGED: Renamed: a capture that changed during transfer now makes the result DATA_UNRELIABLE instead of aborting the read, so the samples are still available for inspection.
errors.DATA_UNRELIABLE: The samples were written to disk but at least one data judgement failed (frozen window, sequence, count, layout anchor, firmware identity or heartbeat). Read verdict.txt for the exact reasons; do not treat array.csv as trustworthy until they are explained.
errors.FRAME_CHANGED: A ping-pong frame sequence changed during one array copy. Retrying in the same running DSS session is allowed; keep the failed copy and verdict for diagnosis.
errors.FRAME_NOT_STABLE: Every requested latest-frame copy overlapped a sequence change. The last CSV is retained with a FAIL verdict. Verify the firmware increments its sequence only after a complete frame, then adjust frame rate or transfer size.
errors.BUFFER_NOT_FROZEN: A frozen-buffer read did not see its declared completion value. The copy may still be available, but its verdict must be FAIL.
errors.MAP_MISSING: A linker map is unavailable. It cannot establish RAM/Flash location; this alone must not prevent an approved download or suppress captured values.
errors.NO_OUT_FILE: The selected output artifact does not exist. Build or select the intended .out, then verify the exact path before a download.
errors.NO_CCXML: No target configuration was selected or found. Supply -Ccxml or create the project target configuration; this is a command/setup problem, not a data verdict.
errors.NO_PROJECT: -ProjectPath does not contain a .cproject file. Select the actual CCS project directory.
errors.NOTHING_SELECTED: init_firmware_contract.ps1 was called without any module switch but that state is unreachable in the default-all path; if seen, re-run without switches or name a module explicitly. Parameter error, exit 2.
errors.BAD_SECTION_NAME: init_firmware_contract.ps1 -DmaSection is not a valid C/linker section identifier. Pass a plain name such as ramgs1 that exists in the project .cmd. Parameter error, exit 2.
errors.BAD_IDENTIFIER: A generated symbol name (array or gate) is not a valid C identifier. Pass names matching ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$. Parameter error, exit 2.
errors.BAD_FW_ID: init_firmware_contract.ps1 -FwId must look like 0x00010001UL. Leave it empty to get a fresh unique value. Parameter error, exit 2.
errors.DMA_SECTION_MISSING: init_firmware_contract.ps1 could not find the requested DATA_SECTION name in any .cmd under the project. A section name that does not exist silently misplaces the array (measured: BuffB all zero), so generation is refused. Add the section to .cmd or pass an existing -DmaSection.
errors.CCXML_INCOMPLETE: set_probe.ps1 refuses to rewrite a .ccxml that lacks a connection instance, a device instance, or <platform>. This guard was added 2026-11-18 because the old script rebuilt the whole file and dropped the <device> node (partnum + ICEPick_C router + Subpath) and 3 of 4 drivers, so DSS openSession reported 'invalid processor ID / Can't generate board data file'. Restore a complete .ccxml (CCS creates it; a .bak may exist) before switching probe type. The rewrite is now minimal-edit and test_set_probe_bruteforce.ps1 asserts no node is lost.
errors.TARGET_BUSY: The target lock names its holder pid, and Enter-TargetLock deletes the lock automatically when that process no longer exists, so a crashed run cannot lock the project permanently. If it persists, the named pid really is alive: one operation at a time.
errors.ITERATE_IN_PROGRESS: The iterate marker is honoured only while the pid it names is alive (Get-IterateMarker checks it), so a crashed continuous run does not block later reads or downloads. The marker file may remain; that is history, not an owner.
errors.READONLY_IN_ITERATE: A continuous run is re-downloading every round, so an attached read would describe a run that is already gone. Wait for the loop to finish, then read the session it leaves behind.
